brief: A 16-second widescreen ad for Petal & Stem, a small neighbourhood flower shop: the florist opens the shop at dawn and arranges a bouquet, then hands it to a smiling customer at the door; warm, natural light; end on the shop front.

chunk-1.prompt: Photorealistic widescreen 16:9 ad with warm, natural light. A florist opens Petal & Stem at dawn, arranges a bouquet, and hands it to a smiling customer at the door. Same people, place and product throughout. The florist wears a cream shirt and sage apron. The customer wears a tan jacket. The shop is a small neighbourhood flower shop with a painted green door and wooden sign. The shop matches @shop. The bouquet is one set of pink and cream flower stems, initially loose, then gathered and wrapped in kraft paper. 0–4 s: At dawn, a medium exterior tracks the florist approaching from outside, unlocking and opening the shop’s front door. Warm natural light catches the apron; the sign stays out of frame. 4–9 s: Cut inside to a close view of the florist’s hands gathering loose stems into one bouquet and wrapping it in kraft paper. A gentle push-in follows the work in warm natural window light. 9–13 s: Cut to a medium doorway two-shot: the florist hands that same wrapped bouquet to the smiling customer, who takes it securely. Warm dawn light falls across both faces; the sign remains outside the frame. 13–16 s: Cut to a steady, straight-on wide exterior of the neighbourhood shop front in warm natural dawn light. Hold the complete façade, with “Petal & Stem” clearly legible above the door. Wherever it is legible the lettering reads exactly "Petal & Stem", every letter right. No readable text except the final shop sign; no speech, voiceover, or music; no duplicate bouquet; always held or resting; silent: no speech, no voiceover.

gate_log.brief: A 16-second widescreen ad for Petal & Stem, a small neighbourhood flower shop: the florist opens the shop at dawn and arranges a bouquet, then hands it to a smiling customer at the door; warm, natural light; end on the shop front.

gate.why: The brief describes an invented ad scenario; Petal & Stem has no specified real-world identity or storefront that must be reproduced.

story.style: 16-second widescreen live-action ad; close-ups and a gentle pullback, with warm, natural dawn light.
story.story:
Dawn light falls across Petal & Stem on Alder Street. Mara, wearing a green apron, unlocks the Petal & Stem door with a brass key and pushes it open. A brass doorbell gives a bright ring.

Inside Petal & Stem, quick close-ups follow Mara’s hands over a wooden counter. Mara gathers pink tulips and white daisies into a bouquet, folds cream paper around the stems, and ties a blue ribbon around the cream paper. Sunlight catches the petals as Mara lifts the bouquet from the wooden counter.

At the Petal & Stem door, Eli smiles. Mara places the bouquet into Eli’s waiting hands. Eli curls both hands around the cream paper, with the blue ribbon hanging over Eli’s fingers.

The camera draws back onto Alder Street. The final shot holds on the Petal & Stem shopfront in warm dawn light. Above the open Petal & Stem door, the shop sign reads: “Petal & Stem.”
story.title: Petal & Stem at Dawn

rules: Prompt first: the whole piece is written as one prose prompt with timestamps; it is cut into chunks only when it is longer than one generation (ltx-2.5 60 s, minimax-h3 30 s) or --clips forces it, at beat boundaries.
Each chunk's prompt = the shared lines (look, subject, the descriptions of the elements in it, exact words, the "no"s) + its beats retimed from 0.

Asset bank, for seeding only: the first appearance of something that must look specific. Seeds come from, in order: (1) the user's materials; (2) found real-world photos (Wikimedia Commons search + vision pick, composer/assets) when the research gate (composer/story) says a real thing appears; (3) a still made on qwen-image-2.1, yes/no-checked, only for what must be exact and cannot be found (a fictional shop's sign). Nothing else is painted.

Every other reference comes from earlier frames: for chunk k>1, the frames of earlier chunks at the seconds the state says an entity was seen are searched; the clearest is vision-confirmed and attached as @name.
Chunk k>1 also gets @previous: the last frame of chunk k-1, or the latest earlier frame that passes the state checks.
Model: ltx-2.5 when no chunk carries a reference; minimax-h3 otherwise. Audio off unless the brief asks for sound.

After each chunk: yes/no questions at each beat's timestamp (is each expected entity there?) and over the whole chunk (exact text everywhere, one product, the same people, the ending); one regeneration with the failure named if a required check fails, within the run's budget.
ffmpeg joins only when there is more than one chunk.
